option_description: Controls whether the registry permits unauthenticated (anonymous) docker pull operations without requiring any credentials. When enabled, any network-reachable actor can retrieve image manifests and layer blobs without presenting a token or password.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires the unauthenticated_registry_access exposure whenever anonymous_pull_enabled is true, regardless of network_exposure value — meaning even an internal registry with anonymous pull enabled is flagged. On a public registry this is a critical finding enabling secret exfiltration from embedded layers (T1552.002). Anonymous pull also combines with missing_pull_rate_limiting_and_abuse_controls: if pull_rate_limiting_enabled is also false, brute-force and resource-exhaustion attacks become trivial (T1110).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt an unauthenticated docker pull against the registry to confirm whether credentials are required.
how_to_obtain.command: docker logout <registry-host> && docker pull <registry-host>/<repo>/<image>:latest 2>&1
how_to_obtain.expected_output: If anonymous pull is enabled the image layers download successfully with no authentication prompt. If disabled you receive 'unauthorized: authentication required' or HTTP 401.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the registry v2 API catalog endpoint without credentials using curl to check for anonymous access.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sv https://<registry-host>/v2/_catalog 2>&1 | grep -E 'HTTP|401|200|unauthorized'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: HTTP 200 with a JSON repository list confirms anonymous pull is enabled. HTTP 401 or 403 confirms it is disabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted Docker Distribution (registry:2), inspect the config.yml for auth middleware configuration. Absence of an 'auth' block means no authentication is required.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/docker/registry/config.yml | grep -A 10 'auth:'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A populated 'auth:' section (htpasswd, token, or silly) indicates authentication is configured. A missing or empty auth block means anonymous access is permitted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, query the system configuration API to check the unauthenticated_resource_download setting.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -su admin:<password> https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/configurations | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i unauthenticated
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Response field 'unauthenticated_resource_download.value: true' confirms anonymous pull is enabled. 'false' confirms it is disabled.

typical_values: true (common in developer/internal convenience registries or public hub mirrors)

option_description: Controls whether the registry permits unauthenticated (anonymous) docker push operations without requiring credentials. When enabled, any actor with network access can inject, overwrite, or backdoor image layers without authentication.
security_impact: The Rego policy unconditionally fires unauthenticated_registry_access whenever anonymous_push_enabled is true — no network_exposure qualifier is applied, making this a standalone high-severity finding at any network boundary. This directly enables supply-chain poisoning (T1525) and malicious image injection (T1204.003). Unlike anonymous pull, anonymous push also violates push_permission_scope integrity, effectively overriding any RBAC controls configured elsewhere.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt an unauthenticated docker push to the registry using a test image to confirm whether push credentials are enforced.
how_to_obtain.command: docker logout <registry-host> && docker tag alpine:latest <registry-host>/test/anon-push-check:probe && docker push <registry-host>/test/anon-push-check:probe 2>&1
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Successful push without authentication confirms anonymous push is enabled. An 'unauthorized' or 'denied' error confirms it is disabled. Clean up the test image afterward.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, retrieve the repository policy and check for principal wildcards that grant push (ecr:PutImage, ecr:InitiateLayerUpload) to '*'.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-repository-policy --repository-name <repo-name> --query 'policyText' --output text | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E 'Principal|PutImage|InitiateLayerUpload'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A Principal of '*' combined with push-related actions confirms anonymous push exposure. Scoped principal ARNs indicate proper control.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Docker Distribution, verify the auth middleware is configured and that no 'silly' auth (which permits all) is in use.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -A 5 '^auth:' /etc/docker/registry/config.yml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: auth type 'token' or 'htpasswd' with a populated realm/service indicates push requires credentials. The 'silly' auth type or absent auth block permits anonymous push.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, navigate to Administration > Configuration > Security and verify 'Allow guests to pull from public projects' and anonymous access settings. Also check each project's Member/Access control settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Administration → Configuration → Security tab → review 'Unauthenticated Access' section; then Projects → <project> → Members → verify no anonymous push role exists
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No guest or anonymous principal should appear with Developer (push) or higher role on production repositories.

typical_values: true (occasionally found in air-gapped CI environments with no external exposure, or misconfigured test registries)

option_description: Indicates the network boundary from which the registry API and data endpoints are reachable. 'public' means reachable from the internet, 'internal' means reachable only within the organization network or VPC, and 'restricted' means access is limited to specific known CI/CD or orchestration CIDRs.
security_impact: network_exposure is a multiplier in the Rego policy used across four rules. unauthenticated_registry_access checks it alongside anonymous_pull_enabled — a public anonymous registry is the worst-case scenario. missing_tls_enforcement is especially critical when public-facing. unrestricted_network_exposure fires directly when the value is 'public'. missing_pull_rate_limiting_and_abuse_controls is also conditioned on this value. The attribute determines blast radius: public exposure makes any authentication or TLS misconfiguration exploitable by the entire internet.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a TCP connection from an external host or use an internet-based connectivity checker to determine if the registry port is publicly reachable.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sk --max-time 5 https://<registry-host>/v2/ && echo 'REACHABLE' || echo 'NOT_REACHABLE'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A response (even HTTP 401) from an external network confirms 'public' exposure. A connection timeout or refused error indicates internal or restricted exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For cloud-hosted registries, use cloud CLI tools to inspect security group, firewall, or load balancer rules to determine allowed source CIDRs.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters Name=group-id,Values=<sg-id> --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions' --output json | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E 'CidrIp|FromPort|ToPort'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 in CidrIp for port 443 or 5000 confirms public exposure. Organization-specific CIDRs indicate internal. A whitelist of CI/CD runner IPs indicates restricted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Perform a DNS resolution and GeoIP/ASN lookup on the registry hostname to determine if it resolves to a public or RFC-1918 address.
how_to_obtain.command: dig +short <registry-host> | xargs -I{} sh -c 'echo "Resolved: {}"; curl -s https://ipapi.co/{}/json/ | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E "org|country|ip"'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A public routable IP with an ASN belonging to a cloud provider or CDN indicates public exposure. An RFC-1918 address (10.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x) indicates internal.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCR/Artifact Registry, check IAM policies and VPC Service Controls. For Harbor, inspect the load balancer or ingress controller listener configuration in the Kubernetes namespace.
how_to_obtain.navigation: GCP Console → VPC Service Controls → Access Policies → check if Artifact Registry is within a service perimeter; or Harbor Kubernetes deployment → kubectl get ingress -n <harbor-namespace> -o yaml | grep 'host:'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An ingress with a public DNS hostname and no VPC perimeter indicates public exposure. A private cluster DNS name or VPC-internal endpoint indicates internal.

typical_values: public (Docker Hub mirrors, open-source project registries)
restricted (mature CI/CD pipelines with explicit CIDR allowlisting)

option_description: Controls whether the registry endpoint enforces HTTPS/TLS for all client connections, refusing or redirecting plaintext HTTP requests. This determines whether image manifests, layer blobs, credentials, and tokens are transmitted over an encrypted channel.
security_impact: The Rego missing_tls_enforcement rule fires when tls_enabled is false or null, making this a standalone high-criticality finding (score 8). Without TLS, credentials transmitted to the registry can be intercepted in transit (T1552.002), and image layer blobs can be tampered with via man-in-the-middle attacks. On a public or internal network, plaintext registry traffic is trivially interceptable with passive sniffing tools. TLS must be true before the minimum_tls_version and certificate_valid checks become relevant.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt a plaintext HTTP connection to the registry on port 80 or the configured HTTP port to verify whether it is refused or redirected.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sv http://<registry-host>/v2/ 2>&1 | grep -E 'HTTP|Location|Connected|SSL|TLS|301|302|400'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A 'Connection refused', HTTP 301/302 redirect to HTTPS, or 'HTTP 400 Bad Request' (indicating the server expects TLS) confirms TLS is enforced. A successful HTTP 200 response confirms TLS is NOT enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Confirm that the HTTPS endpoint is active and presenting a certificate using openssl s_client.
how_to_obtain.command: echo '' | openssl s_client -connect <registry-host>:443 -brief 2>&1 | grep -E 'Protocol|Cipher|Verify|depth'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A successful TLS handshake with Protocol, Cipher, and certificate depth output confirms TLS is active. 'Connection refused' or 'ssl handshake failure' indicates TLS is not properly configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted Docker Distribution, inspect the config.yml http section to verify TLS certificate and key are configured.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -A 10 '^http:' /etc/docker/registry/config.yml | grep -E 'tls|certificate|key|addr'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A populated 'tls:' block with 'certificate:' and 'key:' fields confirms TLS is configured. Absence of a tls block with only 'addr: :5000' confirms plaintext operation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, query the system health endpoint over both HTTP and HTTPS and compare responses to determine which protocol the registry accepts.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sk https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/systeminfo | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i 'harbor_version\|with_notary\|registry_url'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON response over HTTPS with registry metadata confirms TLS is enabled and operational.

typical_values: false (development/local registries, legacy self-hosted installations with reverse proxy handling TLS termination incorrectly documented)

option_description: Specifies the oldest TLS protocol version the registry will accept from connecting clients. Versions below TLS 1.2 contain known cryptographic weaknesses. This setting determines the effective encryption strength of all registry client connections.
security_impact: The Rego missing_tls_enforcement rule fires when minimum_tls_version is TLS_1_0 or TLS_1_1, even when tls_enabled is true. TLS 1.0 is vulnerable to BEAST and POODLE attacks; TLS 1.1 lacks AEAD cipher support and has been deprecated by RFC 8996. Both allow credential interception (T1552.002). The acceptable secure values are TLS_1_2 or TLS_1_3. A value of 'unknown' should trigger investigation as the actual supported versions cannot be determined without scanning.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use nmap's ssl-enum-ciphers script to enumerate all TLS versions accepted by the registry endpoint.
how_to_obtain.command: nmap --script ssl-enum-ciphers -p 443 <registry-host> 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'TLS|SSLv|least strength'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output lists each accepted TLS version (TLSv1.0, TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, TLSv1.3) and their cipher suites. Presence of TLSv1.0 or TLSv1.1 sections indicates the minimum version is too low.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use testssl.sh for a comprehensive TLS version and cipher audit against the registry endpoint.
how_to_obtain.command: testssl.sh --protocols --severity HIGH https://<registry-host>:443 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'SSLv|TLS1|WARN|OK|NOT'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Lines showing 'offered' next to TLSv1.2 and TLSv1.3 with 'not offered' for TLS 1.0/1.1 and SSLv3 indicate a secure minimum version configuration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use openssl s_client to explicitly probe whether TLS 1.0 and 1.1 connections are accepted by the registry.
how_to_obtain.command: echo '' | openssl s_client -connect <registry-host>:443 -tls1 2>&1 | grep -E 'handshake|alert|Protocol'; echo '' | openssl s_client -connect <registry-host>:443 -tls1_1 2>&1 | grep -E 'handshake|alert|Protocol'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An 'ssl handshake failure' or 'alert handshake failure' response for both TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1 probes confirms these versions are rejected. A successful handshake indicates they are accepted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For nginx or HAProxy acting as a TLS-terminating reverse proxy in front of the registry, inspect the ssl_protocols or ssl-default-bind-options directive.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'ssl_protocols\|ssl-default-bind-options\|tls_min_version' /etc/nginx/ /etc/haproxy/ /etc/docker/registry/ 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A directive like 'ssl_protocols TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3;' confirms the minimum is TLS 1.2. The presence of 'TLSv1' or 'TLSv1.1' in the directive indicates a weak minimum version.

option_description: Indicates whether the TLS certificate presented by the registry is valid: not expired, issued by a trusted Certificate Authority (or properly anchored self-signed CA), and with a Subject Alternative Name matching the registry hostname. Invalid certificates cause Docker clients to reject connections unless the --insecure-registry flag is used, which disables all TLS validation.
security_impact: The Rego missing_tls_enforcement rule fires when tls_enabled is true but certificate_valid is false or null. An invalid or self-signed certificate without trust anchoring leads operators and pipelines to use --insecure-registry or curl --insecure flags, effectively disabling TLS validation entirely and opening the connection to man-in-the-middle attacks that can intercept credentials (T1552.002) and tamper with image layers in transit. Certificate expiry also causes production outages if not monitored.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the certificate presented by the registry using openssl s_client to check expiry, issuer, and subject alternative names.
how_to_obtain.command: echo '' | openssl s_client -connect <registry-host>:443 -servername <registry-host> 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -issuer -subject -ext subjectAltName 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: notAfter date should be in the future. issuer should be a recognized public CA (Let's Encrypt, DigiCert, etc.) or an internal PKI CA that is distributed to client trust stores. subjectAltName should include the registry FQDN.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use curl with verbose output to verify the full certificate chain validation and check for any certificate warnings.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -sv https://<registry-host>/v2/ 2>&1 | grep -E 'SSL|certificate|expire|issuer|subject|verify|error'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output showing 'SSL certificate verify ok' and 'Server certificate' details with a future expiry confirms a valid certificate. 'SSL certificate problem: certificate has expired' or 'self-signed certificate' indicates certificate_valid should be false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check whether Docker daemon or CI/CD runners are configured to use --insecure-registry, which indicates the certificate is not trusted.
how_to_obtain.command: cat /etc/docker/daemon.json | python3 -m json.tool | grep -i insecure; grep -r 'insecure-registry\|DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY\|--insecure' /etc/systemd/system/docker.service /etc/default/docker ~/.docker/config.json 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Presence of the registry hostname in 'insecure-registries' array or DOCKER_TLS_VERIFY=0 in the environment is a strong indicator that certificate_valid is effectively false in practice.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use testssl.sh to perform a comprehensive certificate validation check including chain completeness and expiry.
how_to_obtain.command: testssl.sh --certificate https://<registry-host>:443 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'expiration|trust|chain|commonName|altNames|WARN|OK|CRITICAL'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All certificate checks showing 'OK' with no WARN or CRITICAL findings confirms certificate_valid is true. CRITICAL for 'expired' or WARN for 'self-signed' indicates false.

typical_values: true (production registries with properly managed certificates)
false (development registries with self-signed certs, expired certificates in neglected environments, registries behind misconfigured TLS-terminating proxies)

option_description: Describes the breadth of identities granted push (write) access to the registry or repository. Values range from tightly scoped pipeline service accounts to broad organizational groups or anonymous principals, indicating how strictly image write access is controlled.
security_impact: The Rego overly_permissive_push_authorization rule fires when push_permission_scope is 'all_authenticated_users', 'wildcard_group', or 'anonymous'. These configurations allow any user in the organization (or the internet) to push images, enabling supply-chain poisoning (T1525) and malicious image injection (T1204.003). This attribute also feeds the tag_mutability_without_immutability_enforcement rule — a 'team_wide' or 'organization_wide' scope combined with mutable tags and no immutability enforcement triggers that finding. The secure values are 'scoped_pipeline_identities' or 'specific_service_accounts'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, enumerate all project members and their roles using the Harbor API to identify any broad groups or roles with Developer (push) access.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -su admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-name>/members' | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E 'entity_name|role_name|entity_type'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Members with role_name 'Developer' or higher should be specific service account names (e.g., 'ci-pipeline-sa') not group names like 'all-employees' or 'authenticated-users'.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, retrieve and analyze the repository policy to determine the effective principal scope for push-related actions.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-repository-policy --repository-name <repo-name> --output text --query 'policyText' | python3 -m json.tool | python3 -c "import sys,json; p=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(s.get('Principal'), s.get('Action')) for s in p.get('Statement',[])]" 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Principals should be specific role or user ARNs for CI/CD pipelines. A Principal of '*' or 'AWS: *' combined with ecr:PutImage, ecr:InitiateLayerUpload actions indicates anonymous or wildcard scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCP Artifact Registry, review IAM bindings on the repository resource to identify who has roles/artifactregistry.writer or higher.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud artifacts repositories get-iam-policy <repo-name> --location=<region> --project=<project-id> --format=json | python3 -m json.tool | grep -A 5 'artifactregistry.writer\|artifactregistry.admin'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Members should be specific service account emails (e.g., ci-runner@project.iam.gserviceaccount.com). allUsers, allAuthenticatedUsers, or domain-wide principals indicate overly broad scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, navigate to each production project's Members tab and review which users, groups, and robot accounts have Developer or higher roles.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Projects → <project-name> → Members → review all entries with Role 'Developer', 'Maintainer', or 'Project Admin'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Only named robot accounts (e.g., 'robot$ci-pipeline') should appear with Developer role. Human user groups or LDAP groups with push access indicate team_wide or organization_wide scope.

typical_values: scoped_pipeline_identities (mature CI/CD pipelines with robot accounts)
all_authenticated_users (common default in newly deployed Harbor or Nexus instances)
team_wide (small engineering teams with shared access)
organization_wide (enterprise registries with insufficient RBAC configuration)

option_description: Indicates whether production-critical image tags such as 'latest', versioned release tags, or environment-specific tags are protected from overwrite through registry-enforced tag immutability, tag protection rules, or an approval-gated promotion workflow.
security_impact: The Rego overly_permissive_push_authorization rule fires when human users or broad groups have push access AND production_tag_overwrite_protected is false. Without this protection, any authorized push identity can silently replace a known-good production image tag with a malicious image (T1525, T1204.003), and orchestration platforms consuming 'latest' will pull the poisoned image on next deployment. This is one of the most common supply-chain attack vectors. The tag_mutability_without_immutability_enforcement rule separately fires when tag immutability is absent, compounding the risk.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, check whether image tag immutability is enabled on production repositories.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr describe-repositories --query 'repositories[*].{name:repositoryName,tagMutability:imageTagMutability}' --output table 2>/dev/null | grep -E 'IMMUTABLE\|MUTABLE\|name'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: IMMUTABLE status for production repositories confirms tag overwrite protection. MUTABLE indicates tags including 'latest' can be overwritten by any authorized push.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, check whether the project has immutable tag rules configured via the API.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -su admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project-name>/immutabletagrules' | python3 -m json.tool
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A non-empty array of immutable tag rules covering production tags (e.g., matching 'v*.*.*', 'release-*', or 'latest') indicates protection is enabled. An empty array [] confirms no immutability rules exist.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GitHub Container Registry (GHCR) or GitLab Container Registry, check branch protection and tag protection rules that govern which CI pipelines can push to specific tags.
how_to_obtain.command: gh api repos/<owner>/<repo>/tags/protection --paginate 2>/dev/null | python3 -m json.tool | grep -E 'pattern|enabled'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Protected tag patterns covering release and production tags indicate overwrite protection. No patterns or an empty response indicates production tags are unprotected.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, navigate to project settings and review Immutable Tags rules. For GCP Artifact Registry, check the tag policies in the repository settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Projects → <project-name> → Tag Immutability → review list of immutable tag rules; GCP Console → Artifact Registry → <repository> → Edit → Tag policies
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Rules matching release patterns (e.g., 'v*', 'prod-*', 'latest') with immutable status confirm protection is enabled. An empty tag immutability list confirms production_tag_overwrite_protected is false.

typical_values: false (majority of self-hosted registries and default cloud registry configurations)
true (ECR repositories explicitly configured with IMMUTABLE tag mutability, Harbor projects with immutable tag rules, mature GitOps pipelines with promotion gates)

option_description: Controls which categories of identity (pipeline service accounts, human users, broad groups, wildcards, or anonymous principals) hold push permissions on the registry or its critical repositories. This attribute captures the identity taxonomy rather than individual principals.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires `overly_permissive_push_authorization` when `human_user` or `broad_group` appears in this array without `production_tag_overwrite_protected` being set. Broad or human push access allows unauthorized parties to overwrite production image tags with malicious content, enabling supply-chain poisoning and lateral movement into production workloads.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, enumerate all IAM principals with ecr:PutImage or ecr:InitiateLayerUpload permissions and classify each by type.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-repository-policy --repository-name <repo> --query 'policyText' | jq . && aws iam list-roles | jq '[.Roles[].RoleName]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON policy documents listing principal ARNs; classify each as service account (*/sa-*, */role/*), human user (*/user/*), group (group ARNs), wildcard (*), or anonymous.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, use the Harbor API to list project members and their roles, then classify by type.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/projects/<project>/members' | jq '[.[] | {name: .entity_name, type: .entity_type, role: .role_name}]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Array of members with entity_type=u (user) or g (group) and role IDs 1=projectAdmin 2=developer 3=guest; developer and admin roles include push.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, navigate to the project's Members tab and filter by roles with push access (Project Admin, Developer). In AWS ECR console, open Repository > Permissions to view the resource policy.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor: Projects > <project> > Members | AWS ECR Console: Amazon ECR > Repositories > <repo> > Permissions
how_to_obtain.expected_output: List of principals and their roles; categorize each as pipeline_service_account, human_user, broad_group, wildcard, or anonymous.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Google Artifact Registry, query IAM bindings on the repository resource to enumerate all principals with roles/artifactregistry.writer or higher.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud artifacts repositories get-iam-policy <repo> --location=<region> --project=<project> --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.role | test("writer|admin"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON bindings listing members; classify serviceAccount: prefixes as pipeline_service_account, user: as human_user, group: as broad_group, allUsers/allAuthenticatedUsers as wildcard/anonymous.

option_description: Indicates whether a signature verification policy (Cosign, Notary v2/TUF) is actively configured and enforced at pull time, blocking unsigned or signature-invalid images from being served to consumers.
security_impact: The Rego rule `image_signing_and_verification_disabled` triggers when this is false. Without pull-time signature enforcement, unsigned or tampered images can be stored and served without integrity validation, enabling supply-chain poisoning via T1553.006 (Code Signing Policy Modification) and T1036.001 (Invalid Code Signature).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for a Cosign ClusterImagePolicy CRD in the Kubernetes cluster to confirm a policy resource exists.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get clusterimagepolicy --all-namespaces -o yaml 2>/dev/null || kubectl get imagepolicy --all-namespaces -o yaml 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more ClusterImagePolicy/ImagePolicy resources present with spec.authorities defined; absence means not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for Connaisseur admission webhook configuration which enforces signature verification.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get validatingwebhookconfigurations -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("connaisseur|cosign|notary|sigstore")) | .metadata.name'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Webhook name matching a signature enforcement tool; empty result means no enforcement webhook is present.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, check Content Trust enforcement under project configuration. In AWS ECR, verify that a Signing Policy is attached via AWS Signer or that an ECR pull-through policy referencing Cosign is active.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor: Projects > <project> > Configuration > Content Trust (checkbox) | AWS ECR Console: Repositories > <repo> > Image Scanning / Signing settings
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Content Trust checkbox enabled (Harbor) or signing policy ARN attached (ECR/AWS Signer).

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Connaisseur Helm values or Cosign policy YAML deployed to the cluster.
how_to_obtain.command: helm get values connaisseur -n connaisseur 2>/dev/null || cat /etc/cosign/policy.yaml 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy file with `policy.mode: enforce` or equivalent; absent file means policy is not enforced.

option_description: Specifies the operational mode of the image signature verification policy: 'enforce' actively blocks non-compliant images at pull time, 'audit' logs violations without blocking, and 'disabled' performs no verification whatsoever.
security_impact: The Rego rule `image_signing_and_verification_disabled` fires when this is 'audit' or 'disabled' even if `signature_verification_policy_enforced` is true. Audit-only mode provides false assurance — unsigned or tampered images still run in production while only generating log noise, failing to prevent T1553.006 supply-chain attacks.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Cosign ClusterImagePolicy spec for the policy mode field.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get clusterimagepolicy -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}: mode={.spec.mode}{"\n"}{end}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each policy name followed by mode=enforce or mode=warn; warn is equivalent to audit. Missing mode field defaults to warn in some versions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect the Connaisseur Helm values file for the detection mode setting.
how_to_obtain.command: helm get values connaisseur -n connaisseur -o yaml | grep -E 'detection_mode|policy.*mode|enforcement'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: `detection_mode: false` means enforce; `detection_mode: true` means audit/log-only.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Notary v2/Ratify, check the Policy Custom Resource for the enforcement action.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get policy.config.ratify.deislabs.io -A -o yaml | grep -E 'action|mode|enforcement'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: `action: enforce` confirms blocking mode; `action: audit` or `action: warn` means non-blocking.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR with Signer policies, check the signing configuration action via the CLI.
how_to_obtain.command: aws signer get-signing-profile --profile-name <profile> --query 'status' && aws ecr get-registry-scanning-configuration --query 'scanningConfiguration'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active signing profile with enforce semantics configured on the registry.

option_description: Indicates whether at least one trusted public key or certificate authority is explicitly bound to the signature verification policy for validating image provenance. Without configured trust anchors, signature verification cannot function even if enabled.
security_impact: The Rego rule `image_signing_and_verification_disabled` fires when `signature_verification_policy_enforced` is true and `signature_enforcement_mode` is 'enforce' but this is false. A policy without trust anchors is effectively inert — any key or no key could satisfy verification, defeating the purpose of signing controls and leaving the supply chain unprotected against T1036.001.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Cosign ClusterImagePolicy authorities to confirm public key references are present.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get clusterimagepolicy -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{.spec.authorities}{"\n"}{end}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-empty authorities array with key.data (PEM public key) or keyless.identities entries per policy; empty authorities means no trust anchors configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check the Connaisseur validators configuration for trust root public keys or certificate references.
how_to_obtain.command: helm get values connaisseur -n connaisseur -o yaml | grep -A 20 'validators:' | grep -E 'trust_roots|key|cert|host'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: One or more trust_roots entries with name and key PEM data present; empty trust_roots means no signing keys configured.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Notary v2/Ratify, check the VerifierStore and Certificate Store CRDs for configured trust anchors.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get certificatestore -A -o yaml | grep -E 'certificates|provider|value' && kubectl get verifier -A -o yaml | grep -E 'trustPolicies|keyRef|certRef'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Certificate stores populated with PEM data or references to secret names; empty stores mean no trust anchors.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS Signer, verify that at least one signing profile exists with a valid certificate and that it is referenced in ECR image signing configuration.
how_to_obtain.command: aws signer list-signing-profiles --query 'profiles[?status==`Active`].[profileName,signingMaterial.certificateArn]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: At least one Active profile with a non-null certificateArn confirming a trusted CA is configured.

option_description: Controls whether automated scanning for hardcoded secrets, API keys, passwords, and certificates is enforced on image layers and history before images are accepted into or served from the registry, via CI gate, admission webhook, or registry-native scanner.
security_impact: The Rego rule `secrets_embedded_in_image_layers` fires when this is false regardless of `image_pull_access_scope`, because even without confirmed secrets the absence of scanning means secrets may be present but undetected. Without layer scanning, credentials embedded in image layers via T1552.001 and T1552.004 are exfiltrable by any pull-authorized client.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, verify the secret scanning interrogation service is configured and enabled for the project.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor: Administration > Interrogation Services > check for Trivy or Anchore integration > Projects > <project> > Configuration > Automatically scan images on push (checkbox)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Scanner listed under Interrogation Services and auto-scan enabled at project level; both must be true for enforcement.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, check if Inspector enhanced scanning is enabled and configured to scan on push for the registry.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-registry-scanning-configuration --query 'scanningConfiguration.{scanType:scanType,rules:rules}' && aws inspector2 list-coverage --filter-criteria '{"ecrImageTags":[{"comparison":"NOT_EQUALS","value":"dummy"}]}' --query 'coveredResources[0].resourceMetadata.ecrRepository.scanFrequency'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: scanType: ENHANCED with rules covering relevant repositories; scanFrequency: SCAN_ON_PUSH confirms push-time scanning is active.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review CI/CD pipeline configuration for a secret scanning gate (e.g., Trivy or TruffleHog step) that blocks image push on findings.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -rE 'trivy.*secret|trufflehog|detect-secrets|gitleaks' .gitlab-ci.yml .github/workflows/*.yml Jenkinsfile 2>/dev/null | head -30
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Pipeline definition contains a secret scanning step with `--exit-code 1` or equivalent failure gate before the docker push step.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check for an admission webhook that invokes secret scanning before allowing image admission into the cluster.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get validatingwebhookconfigurations -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("scan|secret|trivy|anchore")) | {name: .metadata.name, rules: .webhooks[].rules}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Webhook configuration matching registry endpoints with rules covering image operations; empty result means no admission-time secret scanning.

option_description: The count of hardcoded secrets, API keys, passwords, or certificates found embedded in filesystem layers or image history metadata across production images in the registry as reported by the most recent layer scanning run.
security_impact: The Rego rule `secrets_embedded_in_image_layers` fires when this is greater than 0 combined with `layer_secret_scanning_enabled` being false, or when it is greater than 0 with `image_pull_access_scope` set to 'public'. Any nonzero count means confirmed credentials are accessible to pull-authorized principals, directly enabling T1552.001 (Credentials in Files) and T1552.004 (Private Keys) exfiltration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Run Trivy in secret-scanning mode against all production images in the registry and aggregate the finding count.
how_to_obtain.command: for img in $(docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}' | grep -v '<none>'); do trivy image --scanners secret --quiet --format json "$img" 2>/dev/null | jq '.Results[].Secrets | length' 2>/dev/null; done | awk '{s+=$1} END {print "Total secrets detected:", s}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Numeric total of secrets found; 0 means no secrets detected, any positive number requires immediate investigation.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Use TruffleHog to scan a pulled image tarball for high-entropy strings and known secret patterns.
how_to_obtain.command: docker save <registry>/<image>:<tag> -o /tmp/image.tar && trufflehog docker --image file:///tmp/image.tar --json 2>/dev/null | jq 'length'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON array count of findings; 0 is secure, any positive count lists detector type, file path, and raw secret fragment.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR with Inspector enhanced scanning, query the Inspector2 API for SECRET_SCANNING findings across all ECR images.
how_to_obtain.command: aws inspector2 list-findings --filter-criteria '{"findingType":[{"comparison":"EQUALS","value":"SECRET"}]}' --query 'length(findings)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Integer count of Inspector secret findings across ECR; 0 is desired, any positive value indicates embedded secrets.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor with Trivy integration, view the vulnerability/secret scan results for each production repository to count secret findings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor: Projects > <project> > Repositories > <repo> > Artifacts > click artifact > Scan tab > Secrets section
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Secrets count displayed per artifact; sum across all production artifacts gives the aggregate secrets_detected_in_layers value.

option_description: Defines the breadth of principals authorized to pull images from the registry: 'restricted' limits pulls to specific service accounts or roles, 'authenticated_users' allows any authenticated user in the identity domain, and 'public' permits unauthenticated pulls by anyone.
security_impact: The Rego rule `secrets_embedded_in_image_layers` fires when this is 'authenticated_users' or 'public' and `layer_secret_scanning_enabled` is false — because broad pull access combined with unscanned images means any credential embedded in layers is potentially exfiltrable. When set to 'public', even confirmed secrets (`secrets_detected_in_layers > 0`) trigger the rule regardless of scanning status, as public access removes all barriers to T1552.001 exfiltration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, inspect the repository policy to determine if pull permissions are granted to specific roles, all authenticated AWS accounts, or public.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr get-repository-policy --repository-name <repo> --query 'policyText' | python3 -c "import sys,json; p=json.load(sys.stdin); [print(s.get('Principal',''),s.get('Effect','')) for s in p.get('Statement',[])]" 2>/dev/null || echo 'No resource policy (private only)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Principal '*' with Allow Effect = public; Principal {'AWS': '*'} with Condition on account = authenticated_users; specific role ARNs only = restricted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For ECR Public Gallery, check if the repository is public using the ECR Public API.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr-public describe-repositories --query 'repositories[*].[repositoryName,repositoryUri]' 2>/dev/null | head -20
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Any repository listed here is publicly accessible without authentication; absence means no public ECR repositories.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, check project access level to determine public vs. private pull scope.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor: Projects > <project> > Configuration > Access Level: Public/Private toggle | Members tab to verify if 'Guest' role is granted to broad groups
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Access Level: Public = public scope; Private with broad Guest group membership = authenticated_users; Private with specific service accounts only = restricted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Google Artifact Registry, check IAM bindings for allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers on the repository.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud artifacts repositories get-iam-policy <repo> --location=<region> --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.members[] | test("allUsers|allAuthenticatedUsers")) | {role: .role, scope: .members}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: allUsers present = public; allAuthenticatedUsers present = authenticated_users; only specific service accounts = restricted.

option_description: Indicates whether the registry is integrated with an automated container image vulnerability scanner (Trivy, Clair, Anchore, Snyk, or cloud-native equivalents) that scans images on push or pull to detect known CVEs in OS packages and application dependencies.
security_impact: The Rego rule `missing_vulnerability_scanning_integration` fires when this is false. Without scanner integration, images containing exploitable CVEs flow undetected from the CI/CD pipeline into production orchestration, enabling T1525 (Implant Internal Image), T1612 (Build Image on Host), and T1611 (Escape to Host) attack chains. The policy also checks that scanning is not present in name only — `scan_on_push_enforced` and `promotion_gate_cve_threshold` must also be set.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, verify that a scanner (Trivy or Anchore) is configured and set as the default interrogation service.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor: Administration > Interrogation Services > verify scanner listed with green status > Projects > <project> > Configuration > Automatically scan images on push (must be checked)
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Active scanner visible under Interrogation Services; auto-scan checkbox enabled at project level confirms integrated scanning on push.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, verify that Inspector v2 enhanced scanning is enabled and covers the target registry.
how_to_obtain.command: aws inspector2 get-configuration --query 'ecrConfiguration.{rescanDuration:rescanDuration}' && aws inspector2 list-coverage --query 'coveredResources[?resourceType==`AWS_ECR_CONTAINER_IMAGE`] | length(@)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Non-zero coverage count with rescanDuration set (LIFETIME or DAYS_180) confirms Inspector integration; zero coverage means not integrated.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Azure Container Registry, check if Microsoft Defender for Containers is enabled and covering the registry.
how_to_obtain.command: az security pricing show --name Containers --query '{pricingTier: pricingTier}' && az acr show --name <registry> --query 'systemData' | grep -i defender
how_to_obtain.expected_output: pricingTier: Standard confirms Defender for Containers is active; subresource-level scanning coverage confirms registry integration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted registries, check the scanner webhook or API endpoint registration to confirm active scanner integration.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/scanners' | jq '[.[] | {name: .name, url: .url, health: .health}]'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Array with at least one scanner entry having health: healthy; empty array or health: unhealthy means scanner is not effectively integrated.

option_description: Controls whether automatic vulnerability scanning is triggered on every image push to the registry and whether unscanned images are blocked from being pulled or promoted. When enforced, the registry rejects or quarantines images that have not completed a vulnerability scan.
security_impact: The Rego policy fires the missing_vulnerability_scanning_integration exposure when vulnerability_scanner_integrated is true but scan_on_push_enforced is false AND promotion_gate_cve_threshold is none. Without scan-on-push enforcement, vulnerable images can be pushed and immediately pulled into production before any scan completes, creating a window where unvetted content enters the supply chain.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, use the CLI to describe repository scan configurations and check the scanOnPush field for each repository.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ecr describe-repositories --query 'repositories[*].{name:repositoryName,scanOnPush:imageScanningConfiguration.scanOnPush}' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A table listing each repository with scanOnPush as true or false. All production repositories should show true.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, navigate to the target project, open Configuration, and look for the 'Automatically scan images on push' checkbox under Vulnerability settings.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI > Projects > {project-name} > Configuration > Vulnerability > Automatically scan images on push
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Checkbox is checked/enabled for all production projects.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Harbor API to check scan-on-push configuration for all projects programmatically.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:${HARBOR_PASSWORD} https://${HARBOR_HOST}/api/v2.0/projects | jq '.[].metadata.auto_scan'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: All production project entries return 'true'. Any 'null' or 'false' indicates scan-on-push is not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted registries integrated with Trivy or Clair, inspect the registry webhook or scanner integration configuration file for scan triggers.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'scan_on_push\|scanOnPush\|auto_scan' /etc/registry/ /etc/harbor/ 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Configuration key present and set to true or enabled.

option_description: Defines the minimum CVE severity level that automatically blocks an image from being promoted from the registry to production orchestration platforms. When set to 'none', no severity gate exists and images with any CVE severity can be deployed.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers missing_vulnerability_scanning_integration when scan_on_push_enforced is false AND promotion_gate_cve_threshold equals 'none'. Even with scanning enabled, a threshold of 'none' means scan results are informational only and do not prevent vulnerable images from reaching production, neutralizing the protective value of scanning.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect OPA/Gatekeeper admission webhook policies or CI/CD pipeline configuration for CVE severity gate rules applied at image promotion time.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get constrainttemplate,constraint -A -o yaml | grep -i 'cve\|severity\|vulnerability' | head -40
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Policy rules referencing severity levels such as CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM as block conditions.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR with Inspector integration, check the registry-level or pipeline-level policy that gates on scan findings severity.
how_to_obtain.command: aws inspector2 list-findings --filter-criteria '{"severity":[{"comparison":"EQUALS","value":"CRITICAL"}]}' --query 'findings[0].severity' --output text
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Returns severity values. Cross-reference with pipeline break conditions to confirm the gate threshold.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In Harbor, navigate to the project Policy tab and review the CVE allowlist and deployment security policy to identify the configured severity block level.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI > Projects > {project-name} > Policy > Deployment Security > Severity
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A severity dropdown showing the blocking level: None, Low, Medium, High, or Critical.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Interview the CI/CD team and review pipeline YAML files for image promotion stages to identify any CVE severity gate steps implemented via Trivy, Grype, or Snyk.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'severity\|exit-code\|fail-on\|cve-threshold' .github/ .gitlab-ci.yml Jenkinsfile 2>/dev/null
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Pipeline steps specifying a severity threshold (e.g., '--severity CRITICAL,HIGH --exit-code 1') that halts promotion on detection.

option_description: Indicates whether an automated or enforced rotation policy exists for service account credentials, robot accounts, or tokens used by CI/CD pipelines and orchestration platforms to authenticate to the registry. Rotation may be implemented via secrets managers, registry token TTLs, or scheduled automation.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers weak_or_shared_service_account_credentials when credential_scope is 'shared' AND credential_rotation_policy_enabled is false, or when credential_rotation_policy_enabled is false AND credential_max_age_days is 0 (non-expiring). Without rotation, a compromised credential provides indefinite unauthorized registry access, enabling supply-chain poisoning or image exfiltration.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Check AWS Secrets Manager or HashiCorp Vault for rotation schedules applied to registry credentials stored as secrets.
how_to_obtain.command: aws secretsmanager describe-secret --secret-id registry/prod/robot-account --query '{RotationEnabled:RotationEnabled,RotationRules:RotationRules}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: RotationEnabled: true with RotationRules specifying AutomaticallyAfterDays. If RotationEnabled is false, no rotation policy exists.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List Harbor robot accounts and check their expiration settings to determine if token TTLs enforce implicit rotation.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:${HARBOR_PASSWORD} 'https://${HARBOR_HOST}/api/v2.0/robots' | jq '.[] | {name:.name, duration:.duration, expires_at:.expires_at}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Robot accounts with expires_at set to a future date within acceptable rotation window. duration of -1 indicates non-expiring tokens.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the CI/CD secrets management runbook or interview the platform team to determine if credential rotation is manual, automated, or absent.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Documentation of a rotation schedule (e.g., 90-day automated rotation via Vault dynamic secrets or AWS Secrets Manager). No documentation indicates no policy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Kubernetes ExternalSecret or SealedSecret manifests to determine if registry credentials reference a secrets backend with rotation configured.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get externalsecret -A -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.name}{" "}{.spec.refreshInterval}{"\n"}{end}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: ExternalSecret objects with refreshInterval set (e.g., 24h or 720h) indicate automated credential sync from a rotating source.

option_description: Describes whether registry credentials used by CI/CD pipelines and orchestration platform service accounts are shared across multiple pipelines, teams, or environments, or whether each integration has its own dedicated, scoped credential with least-privilege permissions.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers weak_or_shared_service_account_credentials when credential_scope is 'shared' AND credential_rotation_policy_enabled is false. Shared credentials mean a compromise in any one pipeline or service exposes the credential to all other consumers, expanding blast radius. Rotation of shared credentials also requires coordinated updates across all consumers, making rotation operationally difficult and often skipped.

how_to_obtain.instruction: List Harbor robot accounts to determine if a single robot account is referenced by multiple projects or if unique accounts exist per pipeline.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:${HARBOR_PASSWORD} 'https://${HARBOR_HOST}/api/v2.0/robots' | jq '.[] | {name:.name, level:.level, permissions:.permissions[].namespace}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Each robot account scoped to a single project namespace indicates per_integration. A single robot with permissions across multiple namespaces indicates shared.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In AWS ECR, enumerate IAM roles and policies used by pipeline executors to determine if multiple pipelines share the same IAM role for registry access.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam list-roles --query 'Roles[?contains(RoleName,`pipeline`) || contains(RoleName,`ci`)].{Name:RoleName,Arn:Arn}' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Multiple distinct roles per pipeline or service indicate per_integration. A single shared role used by all pipelines indicates shared.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect CI/CD pipeline configuration files and Kubernetes image pull secret references to determine if the same named secret is reused across multiple namespaces or pipeline definitions.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get secret -A --field-selector type=kubernetes.io/dockerconfigjson -o jsonpath='{range .items[*]}{.metadata.namespace}{" "}{.metadata.name}{"\n"}{end}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Unique secret names per namespace or pipeline indicate per_integration scope. The same secret name appearing across multiple namespaces indicates shared credentials.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review the secrets onboarding process with the platform and DevOps teams to understand whether new pipelines receive dedicated credentials or are given access to a shared credential set.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A documented process requiring unique robot accounts or service accounts per pipeline indicates per_integration. A shared password distributed across teams indicates shared scope.

typical_values: shared (most common in small and medium teams)

option_description: Represents the age in days of the longest-lived active registry credential, token, or password currently in use by any pipeline or orchestration integration. A value of 0 indicates that no expiry is configured, meaning credentials are perpetually valid until manually revoked.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers weak_or_shared_service_account_credentials when credential_max_age_days exceeds 90 days, or when credential_rotation_policy_enabled is false AND credential_max_age_days equals 0. Long-lived or non-expiring credentials represent persistent attack surface; a single credential theft provides sustained unauthorized access without time-bounded exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query Harbor robot account creation dates and expiry timestamps to calculate the age of the longest-lived active credential.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:${HARBOR_PASSWORD} 'https://${HARBOR_HOST}/api/v2.0/robots' | jq '.[] | {name:.name, creation_time:.creation_time, expires_at:.expires_at, age_days: ((now - (.creation_time | fromdateiso8601)) / 86400 | floor)}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A list of robot accounts with computed age_days. The maximum value across all accounts is the credential_max_age_days. expires_at of null indicates no expiry (value 0).

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, inspect IAM access keys associated with pipeline users and calculate age from creation date.
how_to_obtain.command: aws iam list-users --query 'Users[*].UserName' --output text | xargs -I{} aws iam list-access-keys --user-name {} --query 'AccessKeyMetadata[*].{User:UserName,KeyId:AccessKeyId,Created:CreateDate,Status:Status}' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Table of access keys with CreateDate. Compute days since creation for active keys. Keys older than 90 days represent elevated risk.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query AWS Secrets Manager for the last rotation date of registry credentials to calculate effective credential age.
how_to_obtain.command: aws secretsmanager list-secrets --query 'SecretList[?contains(Name,`registry`)].{Name:Name,LastRotated:LastRotatedDate,LastChanged:LastChangedDate}' --output table
how_to_obtain.expected_output: LastRotatedDate showing the most recent rotation. Calculate days since last rotation. Null LastRotatedDate with an old LastChangedDate indicates a non-rotating long-lived credential.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Request a listing of all active registry credentials from the secrets management system and identify the creation or last-rotation date of each to find the maximum age.
how_to_obtain.command: vault list secret/registry && vault read -format=json secret/registry/pipeline-token | jq '.data.created_at // .metadata.created_time'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Creation timestamps for each credential. Calculate elapsed days. A missing expiry field or TTL of 0 maps to credential_max_age_days value of 0.

option_description: Describes the network scope from which the registry API and storage endpoints are reachable. 'public' means accessible from the internet, 'internal' means reachable within a corporate or cloud VPC network without further restriction, and 'restricted_trusted' means access is limited to specific approved CIDR ranges such as CI/CD runners and orchestration nodes.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers unrestricted_network_exposure unconditionally when registry_network_exposure_scope is 'public', and also when network_policy_enforced is false AND the scope is not 'restricted_trusted'. Public exposure dramatically increases attack surface by allowing any internet actor to attempt authentication, exploit registry software vulnerabilities (T1190), or conduct brute-force attacks against credentials.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR or a registry hosted behind an ALB, check whether the load balancer or service endpoint has a public IP and verify security group ingress rules.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters 'Name=tag:Name,Values=*registry*' --query 'SecurityGroups[*].{GroupId:GroupId,Ingress:IpPermissions}' --output json | jq '.[] | .Ingress[] | select(.IpRanges[].CidrIp == "0.0.0.0/0")'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty output indicates no public ingress rules. Any result with 0.0.0.0/0 on port 443 or 5000 indicates public scope.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Attempt to reach the registry API from an external network or use an online port scanner to verify whether the registry endpoint responds publicly.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -v --max-time 10 https://${REGISTRY_HOST}/v2/ 2>&1 | grep -E 'Connected|Connection refused|SSL|401|200'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Connection refused or timeout from external network indicates internal scope. A 401 or 200 response from an external IP indicates public exposure.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCP Artifact Registry or GCR, check the IAM policy for allUsers or allAuthenticatedUsers bindings that indicate public exposure.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud artifacts repositories get-iam-policy ${REPO_NAME} --location=${LOCATION} --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.members[] | contains("allUsers") or contains("allAuthenticatedUsers"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: No output indicates no public bindings. Any result indicates at minimum 'internal' or 'public' scope depending on the member type.

how_to_obtain.instruction: In the cloud console for the registry service, navigate to the network settings or VPC configuration to view whether a public endpoint or private endpoint is configured.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console > ECR > Repositories > {repo} > Settings > OR VPC Console > Endpoints > search for ECR endpoint type
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A VPC endpoint with no public DNS alias and security groups restricting to internal CIDRs indicates 'restricted_trusted' or 'internal'. A public DNS with open ingress indicates 'public'.

option_description: Indicates whether firewall rules, cloud security group policies, or Kubernetes NetworkPolicy objects are in place that explicitly restrict inbound access to registry API and storage endpoints to known approved CIDR ranges, such as CI/CD runner subnets and orchestration node pools, with a default-deny posture.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers unrestricted_network_exposure when network_policy_enforced is false AND registry_network_exposure_scope is not 'restricted_trusted', and also when network_policy_enforced is false AND approved_source_cidr_ranges is empty. Without an enforced network policy, any network-adjacent actor reaching the registry network segment can attempt to interact with the API, enabling credential brute-force, vulnerability exploitation, and unauthorized image pulls.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kubernetes-hosted registries, list NetworkPolicy objects in the registry namespace and verify they include ingress rules with specific CIDR or pod selector restrictions.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get networkpolicy -n registry -o yaml | grep -A 20 'ingress:'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: NetworkPolicy with ingress rules specifying ipBlock CIDR ranges or podSelector matching only CI/CD and orchestration namespaces. Absence of NetworkPolicy objects or an allow-all rule indicates not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS-hosted registries, list security group rules and verify that inbound rules on registry ports reference specific CIDR ranges rather than 0.0.0.0/0.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters 'Name=tag:Name,Values=*registry*' --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions[?ToPort==`443`].IpRanges[*].CidrIp' --output text
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Specific CIDR ranges such as 10.0.1.0/24 for CI runners and 10.0.2.0/24 for node pools. Output of 0.0.0.0/0 indicates policy is not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Inspect Terraform or CloudFormation infrastructure-as-code to verify security group or firewall rules are defined with explicit CIDR allow-lists for registry ports.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -r 'cidr_blocks\|source_ranges\|ipRanges' terraform/ cloudformation/ --include='*.tf' --include='*.yaml' | grep -v '0\.0\.0\.0/0'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Specific CIDR ranges in resource definitions for registry security groups or firewall rules. Presence of 0.0.0.0/0 in any allow rule indicates policy not enforced.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCP, list VPC firewall rules targeting the registry instance tags and verify no allow rules permit traffic from 0.0.0.0/0 on registry ports.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud compute firewall-rules list --filter='targetTags:registry' --format='table(name,direction,sourceRanges,allowed)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Firewall rules with sourceRanges limited to known internal CIDR blocks. Rules with sourceRanges containing 0.0.0.0/0 indicate network_policy_enforced is false.

typical_values: false (default in many cloud deployments without explicit hardening)
true (environments with defined network segmentation and IaC-enforced rules)

option_description: Contains the explicit list of CIDR ranges that are permitted to reach the registry API and storage endpoints, as defined in firewall rules, security groups, or network policies. An empty list indicates no allowlist has been configured, meaning access is either fully open or controlled only by authentication without network-layer restrictions.
security_impact: The Rego policy triggers unrestricted_network_exposure when network_policy_enforced is false AND approved_source_cidr_ranges is empty. An empty CIDR allowlist combined with no network policy means there is no network-layer defense-in-depth; the registry relies solely on authentication controls. If authentication is bypassed or credentials are stolen, there is no network boundary preventing access from arbitrary sources.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Extract all allowed ingress CIDR ranges from AWS security groups associated with the registry service, filtering for registry ports.
how_to_obtain.command: aws ec2 describe-security-groups --filters 'Name=tag:Name,Values=*registry*' --query 'SecurityGroups[*].IpPermissions[?contains(`[443,5000,8080]`,to_string(ToPort))].IpRanges[*].CidrIp' --output json | jq 'flatten | unique'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON array of CIDR strings such as ["10.10.0.0/16","10.20.1.0/24"]. An empty array [] or ["0.0.0.0/0"] indicates no meaningful allowlist.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Kubernetes-hosted registries, extract ipBlock CIDR values from NetworkPolicy ingress rules in the registry namespace.
how_to_obtain.command: kubectl get networkpolicy -n registry -o json | jq '[.items[].spec.ingress[].from[].ipBlock.cidr] | flatten | unique | map(select(. != null))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An array of approved CIDR blocks. An empty array indicates no IP-based ingress restrictions are defined in NetworkPolicy.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Parse Terraform state or IaC configuration to extract the complete set of CIDR ranges allowed to reach registry security groups or firewall rules.
how_to_obtain.command: terraform show -json | jq '[.. | objects | select(.type=="aws_security_group_rule" and .values.type=="ingress") | .values.cidr_blocks] | flatten | unique'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A deduplicated list of all permitted source CIDRs. This list should correspond to CI/CD runner and orchestration node subnets only.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCP VPC firewall rules, extract all source IP ranges from rules targeting the registry, filtering out deny rules to compile the effective allowlist.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud compute firewall-rules list --filter='targetTags:registry AND direction:INGRESS AND action:ALLOW' --format='json' | jq '[.[].sourceRanges] | flatten | unique'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A JSON array of CIDR ranges permitted to reach the registry. Presence of 0.0.0.0/0 in the list should be flagged even if other specific CIDRs are present.

option_description: Controls whether the backend object storage or block volume (S3, GCS, Azure Blob, LUKS-encrypted disk) used to persist image layer blobs and OCI manifests has server-side or volume-level encryption enabled, typically AES-256 via provider-managed or customer-managed keys.
security_impact: The Rego rule `unencrypted_backend_storage` fires whenever `storage_encryption_at_rest_enabled` is false, raising a host_security finding scored 5. When storage is unencrypted, an adversary who obtains direct storage-layer access (e.g., misconfigured bucket permissions, cloud credential theft) can exfiltrate all image layers and manifests without touching the registry API — bypassing every authentication and authorization control the registry enforces. This directly maps to MITRE T1530 (Data from Cloud Storage) and T1567.002 (Exfiltration to Cloud Storage).

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR-backed or S3-backed registries, query the S3 bucket's server-side encryption configuration using the AWS CLI.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-bucket-encryption --bucket <registry-storage-bucket-name> --output json
how_to_obtain.expected_output: JSON response containing 'ServerSideEncryptionConfiguration' with 'Rules' specifying 'AES256' or 'aws:kms'. If the command returns 'ServerSideEncryptionConfigurationNotFoundError', encryption is not enabled.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCS-backed registries, inspect the bucket's encryption configuration with the gcloud CLI.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud storage buckets describe gs://<registry-bucket-name> --format='json(encryption)'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: A non-null 'encryption' object with a 'defaultKmsKeyName'. An empty or null encryption field indicates Google-managed encryption (enabled by default) or no CMEK; confirm 'defaultEncryption' is present.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted registries using LUKS-encrypted block volumes, verify the volume encryption status on the host.
how_to_obtain.command: lsblk -o NAME,TYPE,FSTYPE,MOUNTPOINT && sudo cryptsetup status <dm-crypt-device-name>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'cryptsetup status' output shows 'type: LUKS2', cipher, and key size. If the device is not a mapped crypt device, encryption is absent.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Azure Blob Storage, navigate to the Storage Account in the Azure Portal and check the encryption settings panel.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Azure Portal → Storage Accounts → <registry-storage-account> → Security + networking → Encryption. Confirm 'Encryption type' shows 'Microsoft-managed keys' or 'Customer-managed keys' and that 'Infrastructure encryption' is enabled if required.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Encryption type is set and the status shows 'Enabled'. A setting of 'Disabled' or absence of the encryption entry indicates a gap.

option_description: Indicates whether the underlying storage backend — S3 bucket, GCS bucket, Azure Blob container, or block volume — is reachable from public networks without requiring registry-level authentication, meaning raw image blobs could be fetched by unauthenticated actors.
security_impact: The Rego rule `unencrypted_backend_storage` includes a compounded condition: when `storage_encryption_at_rest_enabled` is false AND `storage_publicly_accessible` is true, the severity of the finding escalates because unencrypted data is directly internet-accessible. Even when evaluated alone, public storage access bypasses the registry's authentication layer entirely — any actor can enumerate and download OCI blobs directly via the storage provider's endpoint, exfiltrating proprietary code, secrets embedded in layers, and configuration data. This maps to MITRE T1530.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For S3-backed registries, check whether Block Public Access is fully enabled and that no bucket ACL grants public READ.
how_to_obtain.command: aws s3api get-public-access-block --bucket <registry-storage-bucket-name> && aws s3api get-bucket-acl --bucket <registry-storage-bucket-name>
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'BlockPublicAcls', 'IgnorePublicAcls', 'BlockPublicPolicy', and 'RestrictPublicBuckets' should all be 'true'. ACL grants should contain only the bucket owner — any 'AllUsers' or 'AuthenticatedUsers' grantee indicates public access.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For GCS-backed registries, verify that uniform bucket-level access is enforced and the allUsers IAM binding is absent.
how_to_obtain.command: gcloud storage buckets get-iam-policy gs://<registry-bucket-name> --format=json | jq '.bindings[] | select(.members[] | contains("allUsers") or contains("allAuthenticatedUsers"))'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Empty output (no match) confirms public access is not granted. Any matching binding means the bucket is publicly readable.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Azure Blob Storage, query the storage account properties via the Azure REST API to check the public access level on the container holding registry blobs.
how_to_obtain.command: az storage container show --name <registry-container-name> --account-name <storage-account-name> --query 'properties.publicAccess' --output tsv
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output should be 'None'. Values of 'Blob' or 'Container' indicate public read access is permitted.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS S3, use the S3 Console to review the bucket's public access and permissions summary.
how_to_obtain.navigation: AWS Console → S3 → <bucket-name> → Permissions tab. Check 'Block public access (bucket settings)' — all four toggles must be ON. Also review 'Bucket policy' and 'Access Control List' sections for any public grants.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The 'Bucket and objects not public' indicator is shown in green. No policy or ACL entry grants access to '*' or public principals.

option_description: Controls whether the registry platform records an audit trail of all significant lifecycle events — image push, pull, delete, and authentication attempts — to a persistent log destination for security monitoring and forensic investigation.
security_impact: The Rego rule `insufficient_audit_logging` immediately fires when `audit_logging_enabled` is false, raising a host_security finding scored 5. Without an audit trail, there is no mechanism to detect unauthorized image pulls that may have exfiltrated embedded secrets, supply-chain poisoning via unauthorized pushes, or credential stuffing attempts against the authentication endpoint. This absence directly inhibits forensic investigation of all other registry misconfigurations and maps to MITRE T1574.011 (Services Registry Permissions Weakness).

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, verify that CloudTrail is enabled and capturing ECR API calls in the relevant region.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudtrail get-event-selectors --trail-name <trail-name> --region <region> --output json && aws ecr describe-registry --region <region> --query 'replicationConfiguration'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: CloudTrail event selectors should include 'ReadWriteType: All' or at minimum 'WriteOnly'. ECR-specific events (BatchCheckLayerAvailability, PutImage, GetAuthorizationToken) should appear in the trail.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For self-hosted Docker Distribution (registry:2) or Harbor, inspect the registry configuration file for logging settings.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -A 10 'log:' /etc/docker/registry/config.yml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The 'log' section should have 'level: info' or 'level: debug' and 'accesslog: { disabled: false }'. A missing accesslog section or 'disabled: true' means audit logging is off.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, verify audit log settings via the Harbor admin console.
how_to_obtain.navigation: Harbor UI → Administration → Configuration → System Settings. Locate 'Audit log forward endpoint' and 'Skip audit log database' checkbox. Ensure at least one log destination (database or syslog forward endpoint) is configured and the skip option is unchecked.
how_to_obtain.expected_output: An audit log endpoint is configured, or the database storage option is active. The 'Skip audit log database' checkbox is unchecked.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Query the Harbor API to confirm audit log configuration programmatically.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:<password> https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/configurations | jq '{audit_log_forward_endpoint: .audit_log_forward_endpoint, skip_audit_log: .skip_audit_log}'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: 'skip_audit_log.value' should be 'false'. If an audit_log_forward_endpoint is configured, its value should be a valid syslog or webhook URL.

option_description: Specifies the discrete categories of registry events captured in audit logs. The security-relevant set must include 'push' (image uploads), 'pull' (image downloads), 'delete' (image removal), and 'auth' (authentication attempts and failures).
security_impact: The Rego rule `insufficient_audit_logging` fires separately for each missing critical event type: if 'push' is absent, supply-chain poisoning via unauthorized pushes is invisible; if 'pull' is absent, secret exfiltration via image download cannot be detected; if 'auth' is absent, brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks go unrecorded. Each missing category independently triggers the misconfiguration finding scored 5, mapped to MITRE T1574.011.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Docker Distribution (registry:2), inspect the notifications and middleware configuration to see which event classes are forwarded.
how_to_obtain.command: grep -A 30 'notifications:' /etc/docker/registry/config.yml
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The notifications endpoint configuration should include events for 'push', 'pull', and 'delete'. Auth events are typically captured separately via the access log; confirm 'accesslog.disabled' is false.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For AWS ECR, enumerate CloudTrail event names to confirm all relevant ECR API actions are being recorded.
how_to_obtain.command: aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventSource,AttributeValue=ecr.amazonaws.com --max-results 20 --output json | jq '[.Events[].EventName] | unique'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Output array should include 'PutImage' (push), 'BatchGetImage'/'GetDownloadUrlForLayer' (pull), 'BatchDeleteImage' (delete), and 'GetAuthorizationToken' (auth). Missing entries indicate gaps.

how_to_obtain.instruction: For Harbor, retrieve the audit log records to identify which event types are actually being captured.
how_to_obtain.command: curl -s -u admin:<password> 'https://<harbor-host>/api/v2.0/audit-logs?page_size=50' | jq '[.[].operation] | unique'
how_to_obtain.expected_output: The unique operations array should contain 'push', 'pull', 'delete', and 'login'/'auth' equivalent entries. Missing operations indicate those event types are not being logged.

how_to_obtain.instruction: Review raw audit log samples to empirically identify which event categories appear.
how_to_obtain.command: journalctl -u registry --since '24 hours ago' | grep -oP '"action":"\K[^"]+' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
how_to_obtain.expected_output: Distinct action values should include 'push', 'pull', 'delete', and 'authentication' or similar. Absent action types in a registry under normal use indicate those events are not being recorded.

option_description: Defines which metadata fields are captured per log entry. The minimum forensically useful set comprises 'timestamp' (when the event occurred), 'client_identity' (authenticated user, service account, or IP address), and 'image_reference' (repository name with tag or digest).
security_impact: The Rego rule `insufficient_audit_logging` fires three separate times when any of 'timestamp', 'client_identity', or 'image_reference' are absent from log entries — each independently satisfying the misconfiguration condition scored 5. Without 'client_identity', it is impossible to attribute a pull or push to a specific actor. Without 'image_reference', logs cannot confirm which image was accessed or tampered. Without 'timestamp', event correlation and timeline reconstruction for incident response is impossible. All three gaps collectively eliminate forensic utility, mapping to MITRE T1574.011.
